text:
A 2025 review brought together 12 qualitative studies, involving 106 people with psychological difficulties, to understand how they experienced compassion-focused therapy. Overall, the review found a high level of acceptability for the group format. One finding stands out: before starting, some participants saw self-compassion as self-indulgent, weak or lazy.

Why this matters across roles: when someone resists the idea of going easier on themselves, it may not be a lack of motivation. It may be a belief that kindness towards yourself is a failing.

One practical takeaway: if someone brushes off self-kindness, get curious about what they think it would say about them. A question such as "What would it mean about you if you went easier on yourself?" can open the conversation without pushing.

Where the evidence stops:
• These are qualitative studies, so they describe experiences rather than measure outcomes.
• The review covered compassion-focused therapy in clinical populations, and may not reflect other approaches or settings.

Key source: Garrett, Smith and Wittkowski, 2025: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1400962
